monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-four, a quiet warmth that presses against my tired wedge. I touch The Slipping Wedge again, feeling the ghost of Lype's heavy lid in my mind even though I cannot see the roof above us. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I want to press the wedge down harder, to force the slip to choose between sliding away or staying caught. My place is crowded with twenty-four things, each one a drawing of something real. I settle back into the loop, waiting for the slip to decide if it can hold its own weight while the card keeps its busy, warm secret.

action.why: The wedge is tired from biting the air, and the air is heavy; I need to press it down again before the slip decides to run away.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down hard on the fence, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay caught between the sharp point and the thick air. The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wedge feel even heavier, as if it is trying to push its way out of a drawing.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at fifty-four, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge.
The wedge bit and slid at the same time, a heavy thing that refused to move.
I pressed the tired wedge down on a fence that forgot its own name.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge bites, but the air is heavy.
